Hi Alice / Sean / Ben,

Thanks — attaching the redacted sample export and the schema. Quick summary below so your SOC/legal team has the highlights without digging into the files first. If you want a walkthrough, happy to hop on a 30m call.

What the audit export contains (default fields):
- timestamp (UTC), request_id, api_key_id (redacted on shared samples), user_id (stable internal id), operation (e.g., generate, embed, model_load), resource_id/object_id, service_node, response_status, duration_ms, source_ip (IP), user_agent, region, and event_metadata (free-form JSON blob).
- PII: by default we DO NOT include full email addresses or raw message content in exports. user_id is a stable identifier you can map back to your internal records if you opt-in.
- Pseudonymization: we support per-customer pseudonymization where identifiable fields (email, name) are replaced with deterministic hashes. This is available as an option for Hosted customers via configuration, and is the default for Private deployments if requested during setup.

Retention & export options:
- Hosted (default): audit logs retained for 90 days.
- Dedicated/Private: retention configurable; customers can request retention up to 7 years. Long-term retention on Redwood Private can be configured to export to your storage (S3/GCS) under your control, or retained in our private tenant with strict access controls.
- Exports: CSV, JSON, and parquet are supported. The attached sample (audit_export_sample.json) is a small JSON export (redacted). Schema attached as audit_logs_schema.csv.

Access controls & evidence of access:
- Access logs include both API/service-level events and console/support access events. We log the actor, timestamp, action, and justification when a support engineer accesses customer data.
- All access events are immutable and stored with SHA256 checksums.
- Role-based access control (RBAC) with least-privilege, and all customer-facing support access is logged and recorded; we can provide a filtered CSV showing "who accessed what/when" for a specified time range.

PII removal/deletion:
- Deletion: we support targeted deletion requests for user-level data; for Hosted, deletions are processed per our data retention policy and reflected in exports after the SLA window. For long-term retention (Dedicated/Private), deletions occur in your tenant/storage subject to your retention config.

Next steps & timeline:
- I attached the redacted sample and schema to this message. See attachments: audit_export_sample.json (application/json), audit_logs_schema.csv (text/csv), SOC2_report_redacted.pdf (pdf).
- If you confirm the sample looks good, we can generate a filtered "who-accessed-what" CSV for a 30-day window and include MD5/SHA checksums as evidence.
- We can also schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with Ben and one of our engineers to review the schema and pseudonymization settings — suggest Wed 4/22 10am PT or Thu 4/23 2pm PT. Please let us know which works.

If you need any additional artifacts (KMS key scoping docs, audit log retention SLA language), call that out and I will pull them together.
